input.query: How does the synthetic thermal module hold the phase-change salt pack?

features.text: How does the synthetic thermal module hold the phase-change salt pack?

evidence.title: Synthetic phase-change thermal storage module
evidence.quoted_span: A thermal storage module places a sealed phase-change salt pack inside a graphite shell. The shell spreads heat to an aluminum fin array during discharge. The module stores heat from a solar collector for release after sunset.

evidence.title: Synthetic bench study of phase-change heat release
evidence.quoted_span: The synthetic bench study measures heat release from a phase-change salt pack surrounded by a graphite enclosure. A fin array reduces temperature variation during discharge. No outdoor performance is reported.

evidence.title: Synthetic sodium-ion cell and cathode binder
evidence.quoted_span: A sodium-ion cell uses a hard-carbon anode and a Prussian-blue cathode. A water-based binder holds cathode particles on an aluminum current collector. The synthetic test module operates at room temperature.

evidence.title: Synthetic silica aerogel pipe coating
evidence.quoted_span: A silica aerogel layer covers the outside of a stainless steel pipe. A porous ceramic mesh supports the layer and limits cracking during thermal cycling. The coating reduces heat loss in the synthetic test rig.

evidence.title: Synthetic study of reinforced silica coatings
evidence.quoted_span: This synthetic materials study tests a silica aerogel coating on a stainless steel tube. Ceramic mesh reinforcement reduces visible cracks after repeated thermal cycles. The study reports no full-scale installation.
